name: Tessera Industries Phantom Comms Relay PCR-3
product_name: Tessera Industries Phantom Comms Relay PCR-3
description: A covert communications relay device that can be concealed in walls, under floors, or inside furniture, creating a local encrypted mesh network that does not touch any existing communications infrastructure. The PCR-3 creates an independent communication channel between paired devices using frequency-hopping spread spectrum transmission that is virtually undetectable against the background electromagnetic noise of urban environments. Multiple relays can be daisy-chained to extend range, and the network auto-heals if individual relays are destroyed.

specifications.detectability: Below noise floor of standard RF scanners

story_hooks: A sweep of a corporate building found a 15-relay PCR-3 network that had been operating for over a year — someone built a complete covert communications infrastructure inside the building without detection.
PCR-3 relays have been found in public infrastructure — street lights, bus stops, park benches — creating a city-wide covert communication network that anyone with paired devices can access.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flat, rectangular relay module with a minimalist industrial design. The device resembles a thick credit card or small access panel with beveled edges and a slightly domed top surface. Its form factor is deliberately inconspicuous—designed to blend into infrastructure rather than command attention.
physical_description.dimensions: 80mm length × 50mm width × 20mm thickness; approximately the size of a playing card but with notable depth
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and pocketable (~85g); can be easily concealed in clothing, mounted behind wall panels, or hidden within furniture without creating suspicious weight distribution
physical_description.primary_material: Composite biocompatible polymer shell with embedded conductive lattice and frequency-shaping materials. Vasquez Biocompatible signature material—slightly flexible, non-ferrous
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal gray with subtle hexagonal surface texture for RF absorption and to defeat visual detection scanners. Edges show faint iridescent marbling from the embedded metamaterial layer
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary body with muted teal accent running along the spine (indicates active encryption state). Small amber indicator lens recessed into top surface
physical_description.interface_elements: Recessed micro-USB hardwire port on one edge (for permanent power installation or emergency diagnostics). Single amber/green/red status LED under translucent dome (pulsing amber = standby, steady green = mesh active, red = compromised). Barely visible pairing indent on underside for magnetic stack-mounting
distinctive_features: Hexagonal surface micro-texture designed to scatter RF signatures
Iridescent metamaterial visible under oblique angles—shows frequency-shaping engineering
Ultra-low-profile design with no external antennae (integrated internal coils)
Thin spine ridge with embedded conductor path
Recessed status indicator that sits flush when inactive
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tiny Tessera Industries Φ logo (1mm) laser-etched into lower corner. Vasquez Biocompatible stamp molded into back surface. Serial number readable only under UV light. FCC-equivalent GLMZ regulatory compliance markings intentionally vague
physical_description.condition_typical: Often found embedded in drywall, mounted under wooden floorboards, or velcroed inside electrical conduit. In-hand inspection shows slight dust accumulation in texture grooves from urban environment exposure. Battery-powered units may show faint discoloration on underside from thermal cycling
